name: IRLZ44NPBF
title: 55 V, 47 A logic-level N-channel HEXFET power MOSFET in TO-220AB
summary: A single N-channel enhancement-mode power MOSFET of International Rectifier's fifth HEXFET generation, built for logic-level gate drive. It blocks 55 V and carries 47 A continuous with the case at 25 °C, in a lead-free through-hole TO-220AB whose tab is the drain. On-resistance is at most 22 mΩ at VGS = 10 V, 25 mΩ at 5 V and 35 mΩ at 4 V; the threshold lies between 1.0 V and 2.0 V. The junction runs to 175 °C, and the part is rated for avalanche and diode-recovery dv/dt.

circuits.title: Fig 10a: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: Resistive-load switching measurement. A 5.0 V pulse generator drives the gate through RG; RD loads the drain from the VDD supply. VGS is watched at the gate and VDS at the drain, and the four switching times are taken between the 10 % and 90 % crossings of those two waveforms (Fig 10b).
notes: VG.1 and VDD.1 are the positive terminals.

circuits.title: Fig 12a: Unclamped inductive test circuit
circuits.description: Single-pulse avalanche measurement. A 5.0 V gate pulse of width tp, applied through RG, lets current build in L from the VDD supply; when the gate turns off, the inductor drives the drain into avalanche. VDS is taken at the drain and IAS across the 0.01 Ω resistor between the source and the supply return. The drain voltage climbs to V(BR)DSS once tp ends and the current ramps back down to zero (Fig 12b).
notes: VG.1 and VDD.1 are the positive terminals.

circuits.title: Fig 13b: Gate charge test circuit
circuits.description: Gate charge measurement. A 3 mA current pulse charges the gate, and VGS is recorded at the gate (waveform Fig 13a). The drain current is set by a regulator built from a second MOSFET of the same type, whose gate sits at the wiper of a 50 kΩ potentiometer across a 12 V cell. Sampling resistors in the gate and drain returns measure IG and ID.

circuits.title: Fig 14: Peak diode recovery dv/dt test circuit
circuits.description: Body-diode recovery measurement. The device under test has gate and source tied, so only its diode conducts. A driver MOSFET of the same type, switched through RG, sits beneath it, with an inductor from their shared node up to VDD; a current transformer in the test device's source path reports ISD. RG sets the dv/dt and the duty factor D sets ISD. Probe 1 is the driver gate drive (5 V for this logic-level part), probe 2 the diode current, probe 3 the test device's VDS and probe 4 the inductor current, whose ripple stays at or under 5 %.

operation.text: A logic-level part: the threshold is 1.0 V to 2.0 V at 250 µA, and on-resistance is guaranteed at 10 V (22 mΩ), 5.0 V (25 mΩ, 25 A) and 4.0 V (35 mΩ, 21 A). The gate withstands ±16 V. Taking the gate to 5.0 V with 44 V and 25 A at the drain needs at most 48 nC, of which 8.6 nC is gate-source and 25 nC gate-drain (Miller) charge; in Fig 6 the Miller plateau lies near 3 V, and 10 V is reached at about 60 nC.
With a constant gate current, VGS climbs to the plateau while QGS is delivered, stays flat while QGD is delivered, then rises to the drive level VG (5.0 V in Fig 13a); the total is QG.

The 47 A and 110 W figures hold with the case at 25 °C. Dissipation derates at 0.71 W/°C, and at a 100 °C case the continuous current is 33 A; Fig 9 gives the current against case temperature down to zero at 175 °C. Junction to case is 1.4 °C/W max, case to a flat greased heatsink 0.50 °C/W typ, junction to ambient 62 °C/W max. On-resistance at 175 °C is about 2.2 times its 25 °C value (Fig 4).

Single-pulse avalanche energy is 210 mJ from TJ = 25 °C at 25 A in 470 µH with VDD = 25 V and RG = 25 Ω. Repetitive avalanche is rated at 25 A and 11 mJ, limited by maximum junction temperature. The allowed single-pulse energy falls with starting temperature and with current, toward zero at 175 °C (Fig 12c).

The integral diode carries 47 A continuous and 160 A pulsed, drops at most 1.3 V at 25 A, and recovers from 25 A at 100 A/µs in 80 ns typ (120 ns max) with 210 nC typ (320 nC max) of charge. Its forward turn-on is quick enough to ignore beside the delay set by LS + LD. Recovery dv/dt is rated at 5.0 V/ns for ISD ≤ 25 A, di/dt ≤ 270 A/µs.

td(on), tr, td(off) and tf are taken between the 10 % and 90 % levels of the VGS and VDS waveforms (Fig 10b). At VDD = 28 V, 25 A, RG = 3.4 Ω, RD = 1.1 Ω and a 5.0 V gate drive they are 11, 84, 26 and 15 ns typical.
Measured from a point on the lead 6 mm (0.25 in) from the body to the middle of the die contact, the drain inductance is 4.5 nH and the source inductance 7.5 nH typical.
The tab takes a 6-32 or M3 screw tightened to at most 10 lbf·in (1.1 N·m). Leads may be soldered at 300 °C for 10 s, 1.6 mm from the case.

The front face carries the part number, the International Rectifier logo, a date code (one digit of the year, two of the week, then a letter for the assembly line) and the assembly lot code. A P in the assembly-line position marks a lead-free part.
